text:
deploy-bot: :rocket: rollout started for release v2.3.7 to production (canary 10%). Automated health checks: p50 latency +5ms, p95 +52ms, error rate +1.2% over baseline. Condition matched for 'conditional-rollback-policy'. Suggestion: pause canary and auto-revert in 10m unless acknowledged. link: https://ci.redwood.infra/deploy/1775481230 :warning:

sam_oncall: linking graphs now — can we see whether errors are from model calls or infra?

laura_w: quick look: errors are 5xx from runtime-exec on eu-west1 only. us-east looks fine. pattern spikes at T+3m after rollout.

ryan.k: if it's region-scoped we can route traffic away from eu-west1 and continue rollout. But fallback policy currently would revert whole release. I'd vote for pin to v2.3.6 for prod while we triage, unless we can patch region routing quickly.

emma_rm: we should avoid a noisy full revert unless necessary. Proposal: 1) ack to pause auto-rollback, 2) pin traffic away from eu-west1 (temporary), 3) run a targeted revert for eu-west1 if routing not possible within 7 minutes, 4) comms draft to customers if we take >30m. Thoughts?

sam_oncall: I can do the regional routing switch now. Command: `redwoodctl traffic set --region eu-west1 --weight 0` then `redwoodctl rollout resume --canary 10` to continue. If routing fails, I'll execute a manual revert to v2.3.6: `redwoodctl deploy revert --to v2.3.6 --reason "error spike eu-west1"`

laura_w: confirm that no data migrations were included in v2.3.7?

emma_rm: no migrations in this release. safe to revert. I'll hold auto-rollback and notify SRE and PMs. Sam, please proceed with routing. I'll update #prod-incidents with the plan.

ops-bot: Auto-rollback paused by: @emma_rm. Timer cleared.

sam_oncall: routing change applied — eu-west1 now 0% for canary. Monitoring: error rate in eu-west1 dropping as expected. resuming canary at 10% in remaining regions.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: canary resumed (regions: us-east, us-west). Observability: p95 normalized, global error rate back within 0.2% of baseline.

ryan.k: nice. Recommend we're still conservative: pin production default to v2.3.6 for now and do a staged re-rollout once root cause confirmed. Can we lock the version in the deployment service?

emma_rm: creating short lived pin ticket now and will set a manual block on v2.3.7 rollout (release-control: block-until root-cause). I'll own comms if we escalate.

laura_w: created a perf alert ticket and assigned to infra-team. link: https://tickets.redwood/INC-4821

sam_oncall: closing loop — no full revert executed. manual actions: paused auto-rollback, routed eu-west1 off, resumed canary. If any new spike in remaining regions, we execute `redwoodctl deploy revert --to v2.3.6 --reason "global spike after routing" --force` and notify customers.

emma_rm: agreed. Follow-up: postmortem owner assigned to laura_w, target write-up EOD tomorrow. I'll also add a note to the release notes: "v2.3.7 rollout paused for regional runtime errors; fix in progress."

deploy-bot: :information_source: status update: no revert executed. current release version: v2.3.7 (partial: 2 regions), pinned for full-prod until RCA. Monitoring window extended +60m.

ryan.k: :thumbsup: good play. Let's capture the rollback criteria we used here for the runbook (region-only error spike -> prefer routing over global revert).

emma_rm: adding to runbook now. tag: #runbook/deploy-rollback-rules

sam_oncall: will stand by for final signoff.

laura_w: will post initial findings in the ticket in 20m.
